question_text: Draw the low-side NFET current and V_DS voltage waveforms in a synchronous buck converter, alongside the high-side gate signal.
answer_text: The low-side FET conducts (triangle ramp down) exactly when the high-side gate is LOW. Its V_DS is equal to V_in when OFF, and ~0V when ON.
explanation_text: The low-side NFET replaces the diode. When the high-side FET is ON, the low-side FET is OFF and must block the full input voltage (V_in). When the high-side FET turns OFF, the low-side FET turns ON to carry the freewheeling inductor current. Because its R_DS(on) is so small, its voltage drop is practically 0V while conducting.
bonus_question_text: What specification must be extremely low on the low-side FET to prevent switching losses during the dead-time?
bonus_answer_text: The reverse-recovery charge (Q_rr) and forward voltage drop (V_f) of its internal body diode.
